newsitem.title: USA: Clinton lawyer says lawsuit settlement unlikely.
newsitem.headline: Clinton lawyer says lawsuit settlement unlikely.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's lawyer said on Tuesday it is "most unlikely" that the president would agree to an out-of-court settlement of a sexual harassment lawsuit brought against him by Paula Jones.
"The likelihood of a settlement is most unlikely because the president did nothing wrong," Clinton's lawyer Robert Bennett said in an interview on CNN.

"The president denies the allegations of the complaint and has no recollection of ever meeting Paula Jones," Bennett said, adding, "I think that when all is said and done, the embarassment will be on the side of Paula Jones."
The nine-member court on Tuesday unanimously rejected Clinton's claim that a sitting president enjoys temporary immunity from civil lawsuits until after leaving office.

Jones accuses Clinton of making unwanted advances toward her in 1991 he was governor of Arkansas and she was a state employee. Clinton denies the allegations. The Supreme Court made no ruling on the merits of her case, but said it should be allowed to proceed.
"We thought we would get some sort of a mixed ruling ... but I am pleased with some of the language in the decision ... I'm not worried at all," Bennett said.
